elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) is retained verbatim: "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment ... equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance ... divided by two", and 4.2(c) retains the eight-instalment payment mechanic. A capped but live Customer-payable stipulated sum remains, so the preferred no-LD outcome is not achieved.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is triggered solely by "the event the Company terminates this Agreement" (4.2(a)), and the new sentence provides it "shall be the Company's sole early termination fee and the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement", so no other Customer-payable liquidated amount survives.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: "The Termination Payment shall not exceed the fees payable by the Company pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date" — an express three-months-of-fees ceiling tied to the operative fee clause, overriding the retained 4.2(a) formula.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Express words: "and the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement" (Company = Customer; HDI = Vendor/Host).

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the added sentence supplies the three-months-of-Section-3.1-fees cap, the sole-early-termination-fee characterisation and the sole-liquidated-amount exclusivity in operative language, not merely in the margin comment.

Preferred level is not met and correctly not claimed: the Customer-payable Termination Payment, its 4.2(a) formula and the 4.2(c) instalment mechanic all remain, so the result is neither unconditional nor formula-free.

Minimal: a single inserted sentence, no deletion or paraphrase of the retained 4.2(a) computation, 4.2(b) zero-value determination or 4.2(c) quarterly instalments, and no extras (no survival tail, no procedure, no added damages categories, no expense allocation) beyond the three selected elements.

Preserves intent: the cap operates as a ceiling on, not a replacement of, the retained computation, so the 4.2(b) zero-or-negative determination still functions and the amount remains determinable; the eight quarterly instalments in 4.2(c) run against the capped figure without contradiction, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Minor, non-blocking drafting point for the drafter: the rendered insertion carries no "(d)" paragraph designation even though the comment describes it as new Section 4.2(d) — add the subsection label on execution so the reference in the comment matches the instrument.
